California Financial Code 22303 caps interest rates on consumer installment loans under $XXXX at 36% APR. The 179.00% APR reflected in the alleged loan agreement is nearly five times this statutory cap. California Financial Code 22651 renders loans made in violation of this cap void meaning no person has the right to collect principal, charges, or recompense on the loan.

On XXXX XXXX XXXX one week after the alleged loan was purportedly originated the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX entered a Settlement Agreement against XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX License No. XXXX, citing violations of California Financial Code Sections 22303, 22304, 22304.5, 22305, and 22320.5 the exact provisions governing the rate cap applicable to this alleged obligation. NCA'S VALIDATION RESPONSE WAS INADEQUATE TWICE

On XXXX XXXX XXXX I sent NCA a formal written validation demand via certified mail (delivered and signed for XXXX XXXX XXXX, tracking number XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX), disputing the validity of this alleged debt in its entirety and citing the FDCPA, the California Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, and the void nature of the underlying obligation under California law. narrative: Subject : Complaint Regarding Refinance Loan Misunderstanding of Loan Terms and Request for Resolution I am submitting this complaint because I believe there was a significant misunderstanding during my refinance process that resulted in a loan I would never have knowingly accepted. My intention when I applied for the refinance was to refinance my existing loan and receive {$15000.00} in additional funds. Throughout the application process, I believed that was the purpose of the refinance. I provided my pay stubs and banking information because I believed those documents were necessary to qualify for the additional funds I was requesting. After the loan funded, I discovered that I did not receive the {$15000.00}. When I contacted SoFi, I was informed that my application did not include a request for any additional cash and that I had only applied to refinance my existing balance. Although I understand that the signed loan documents indicate no cash proceeds, I signed those documents under the mistaken belief that I was receiving the additional {$15000.00}. Had I understood that I would receive no funds, I would never have agreed to replace my existing loan with one that carried a higher interest rate, a higher monthly payment, and significantly higher total interest costs. My concerns are as follows : My original loan balance was refinanced into a new loan with essentially the same principal balance. I received no cash proceeds from the refinance. My interest rate increased substantially. My monthly payment increased. The total amount of interest I will pay over the life of the loan increased by approximately {$6000.00}. I do not understand why my income documentation and banking information were requested if no additional funds were ever being requested or disbursed. I do not understand how this refinance benefited me in any way, as I assumed greater financial obligations without receiving the {$15000.00} that I believed I was applying for. I fully acknowledge that I signed the loan documents. However, my complaint is that I misunderstood what I was signing. My intent was never to refinance into a more expensive loan without receiving any financial benefit. If I had understood that the application did not include a request for the {$15000.00} and that I would receive no proceeds, I would not have completed the transaction. I respectfully request that SoFi conduct a thorough review of my application, the communications surrounding the refinance, and any recorded telephone conversations or internal notes that may help determine how this misunderstanding occurred. I am requesting that SoFi consider an equitable resolution, including reviewing whether the refinance can be reversed or whether another reasonable solution can be offered to address the misunderstanding and the financial harm I have experienced. I appreciate the CFPB 's assistance in reviewing my complaint and helping facilitate a fair resolution. Thank you for your time and consideration. XXXX XXXX

To date, I have not received any such notice despite the repossession already being reported to the credit bureaus. I am also concerned about the accuracy and completeness of the information being furnished to the consumer reporting agencies. Written proof that all legally required post-repossession notices were mailed or otherwise properly delivered to me, including the date of mailing, the address used, and copies of the notices. XXXX. XXXX. A complete written explanation of Royalty Finances compliance with all applicable federal and state laws governing repossession, post-repossession notices, and credit reporting. I respectfully request that the CFPB ensure Royalty Finance provides a complete written response supported by documentation rather than general statements. If the required notices were mailed, I request documentary proof of mailing. If they were not provided, I request that Royalty Finance take appropriate corrective action, including reviewing the accuracy of its credit reporting and any future collection activity related to this account. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I appreciate the CFPBs assistance in ensuring that consumers are treated fairly and that lenders comply with all applicable consumer protection laws.

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding the continued reporting, furnishing, publication, processing, and verification of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, unverifiable, and legally noncompliant information on my consumer report. The conduct described herein constitutes violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ), including but not limited to FCRA 602, 604, 607 ( a ), 607 ( b ), 611, 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ), 623 ( a ) ( 2 ), 623 ( a ) ( 8 ), 623 ( b ), 605B, and all applicable federal consumer protection requirements. The furnisher and/or consumer reporting agency has failed to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy as required by FCRA 607 ( b ), failed to conduct a lawful and reasonable reinvestigation under FCRA 611 ( a ), failed to review all relevant information submitted by the consumer, failed to properly identify the source and method of verification, failed to provide competent evidence supporting the continued reporting of the disputed information, and continued to publish information that is inaccurate, misleading, incomplete, and damaging. The continued reporting of disputed information without competent documentary evidence raises serious concerns regarding compliance with FCRA 607 and 611, the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act where applicable, the Consumer Financial Protection Act, and all related federal and state consumer protection statutes. Upon information and belief, the furnisher and/or consumer reporting agency has engaged in automated, superficial, and legally deficient dispute processing practices rather than conducting the reasonable investigation required by law. The reporting of information that can not be fully verified through original business records, account-level documentation, complete payment history records, signed contracts, and competent evidentiary support is unlawful and must cease immediately. The burden of accuracy rests upon the reporting entity and not upon the consumer. Any representation that disputed information has been verified without providing a lawful basis for such verification is insufficient under the FCRA. Furthermore, any failure to correct, delete, suppress, or block inaccurate information after receiving notice of dispute constitutes continued publication of potentially false information and exposes the responsible parties to liability for negligent and willful noncompliance under FCRA 616 and 617. The continued reporting of inaccurate information causes substantial harm, including damage to reputation, loss of credit opportunities, higher interest rates, denial of housing opportunities, emotional distress, and financial injury. I demand a complete CFPB-supervised investigation, disclosure of all procedures used to verify the disputed information, identification of every party involved in the verification process, disclosure of the date and method of verification, disclosure of all records relied upon during the investigation, and immediate deletion of any information that can not be fully substantiated through competent documentary evidence. If the information can not be verified in strict compliance with federal law, it must be permanently deleted and removed from all consumer reporting databases. I further request that the CFPB require the responsible entities to fully comply with all obligations imposed under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, the Consumer Financial Protection Act, and all applicable federal and state consumer protection laws and regulations. The only acceptable resolution is the immediate deletion, correction, suppression, or permanent removal of all inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, unverifiable, or unlawfully reported information and full compliance with all consumer protection requirements.

narrative: Over the past several years, I have repeatedly received emails from Affirm stating that suspicious activity was identified on my account and that my account was frozen, with instructions to call Affirm to unfreeze your account. Each email implies that if I call, my account can be unfrozen. I have called multiple times and completed all requested identityverification steps. Most recently, phone representatives told me that Affirm could not verify my identity, my account was locked, my account was ineligible for recovery, and there was no appeal or recovery process available. I was told this decision was final. Because this conflicted with the please call to unfreeze emails, I contacted Affirm customer care by email. A representative XXXX XXXX XXXX then wrote that my account is active on Affirms end and instructed me to call customer service again for assistance. This directly contradicts what I was told by phone. After I pointed out the contradiction in writing and asked for clarification, the same representative later wrote that, after a final security review and exhausting all available recovery protocols, Affirm is unable to restore access to my account. No concrete reason was provided beyond generic references to security and privacy, and there is still no appeal process. At the same time, I continue to receive automated emails telling me to call to unfreeze the account. The only plausible explanation I have been able to identify is that Affirms systems may not have properly updated when I transitioned from using an ITIN ( Individual Taxpayer Identification Number ) to a Social Security number. That is a normal status change for consumers in the United States, and I should not be effectively banned from using a major payment service because Affirm has not reconciled its own records. I have specifically asked whether an ITINtoSSN mismatch is the issue and requested a review, but Affirm has not answered that question or offered a way to correct it. Because Affirm repeatedly references security and identity verification without explaining what is wrong, I now have legitimate concerns that there may have been an attempt at identity theft or some other misuse of my personal information connected to my Affirm profile. I specifically asked representatives on the phone whether there was any indication of identity theft or fraud and whether any steps were being taken to protect me, but they refused to provide details or guidance. Without clear information, I can not tell whether I am dealing with an internal record mismatch ( for example, related to my ITINtoSSN transition ) or an actual identitytheft issue, which is extremely concerning. In summary, Affirm has : Provided conflicting information about whether my account is active, frozen, or permanently restricted. Stated that my account is ineligible for recovery with no appeal, while continuing to send call to unfreeze messages. Refused to give a specific explanation of what information could not be verified or how I can resolve the issue. I am not asking the CFPB to require Affirm to approve any particular loan. I am asking that Affirm be required to provide transparency, consistency, and a genuine opportunity to resolve whatever issue exists with my account and personal information

Specifically, I ask that Cherry review whether I was provided with meaningful disclosures and whether I was able to provide informed consent to the financing agreement under the circumstances. I also request copies of all records related to my loan, including the signed agreement, electronic signature records, disclosures that were presented to me, and any documentation Cherry relied upon in denying my dispute. I believe this matter deserves further review because I expressly requested an explanation before signing, informed the dental office that I was having difficulty understanding the agreement, and was in the midst of mental and neurological treatment at the time. My concern is that I entered into a significant financial obligation without fully understanding its terms despite asking for assistance. I respectfully request that the CFPB review this complaint and facilitate a response from Cherry. I would like Cherry to reconsider its denial, investigate whether the financing agreement was entered into under circumstances that prevented me from giving informed consent, and work toward an equitable resolution. I have attached or will provide supporting documentation, including my dispute correspondence with Cherry, the financing agreement, relevant dental records, and any available medical documentation relating to my condition at the time the agreement was signed.

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
narrative: I am submitting this complaint to request correction and resolution of inaccurate and unverified information currently appearing on my consumer credit report. Several items being reported are incorrect, incomplete, or lack proper verification, including inaccurate payment history, unauthorized inquiries, collection reporting without sufficient documentation, and incorrect personal information. These errors are negatively impacting my credit profile and do not meet the legal standards required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), consumer reporting agencies are required to follow reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy. The continued reporting of inaccurate late payments, unverified accounts, and incorrect personal data demonstrates a failure to comply with this obligation. I previously disputed these items directly with the credit reporting agency and/or furnishers and requested proper investigation and documentation. However, the reporting remains unchanged, and I have not received adequate proof validating the accuracy of the disputed information. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681i, credit reporting agencies must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and delete or correct any information that can not be verified. In addition, any credit inquiries reported without proof of permissible purpose violate 15 U.S.C. 1681b and must be removed. Furnishers also have a duty under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 to report complete and accurate account information. Late payments or derogatory marks reported without documentary support are inaccurate and misleading.

product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
narrative: On XX/XX/year>, I was the victim of an online impersonation scam. I immediately contacted Wells Fargo the same day to report fraud on my account. I informed the bank that I had been deceived into sending money and asked them to block all activity. At that time, I did not see any pending wire transfer in online banking, and Wells Fargo did not disclose that a {$1000.00} domestic wire had been initiated. From XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, my full account balance remained visible with no indication that a wire was pending or processing. Because Wells Fargo did not disclose the pending wire and the balance never changed, I reasonably believed the wire had failed. The bank instructed me only to call back Monday, and no fraud XXXX contacted me. On XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo closed my account due to the fraud report and transferred the full visible balance into a new account. Again, no pending wire was disclosed to me before the closure, and the full balance was moved as if no outgoing transfer existed. XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX day after the account was closed and XXXX days after I reported fraud, the {$1000.00} wire posted. This was the first time I became aware that the wire had gone through. I immediately contacted Wells Fargo again, and only then did the bank open a fraud claim. Wells Fargo later denied the claim, stating the wire was authorized, but this ignores several critical facts : This is a wire transfer dispute involving fraud and deception. The bank misclassified the transfer as authorized even though I acted under impersonation and coercion. I reported fraud before the wire posted. Wells Fargo failed to disclose the pending wire during multiple calls. Wells Fargo failed to act after fraud notice and did not escalate the case. Wells Fargo allowed a pending wire to post after account closure. The bank ignored deception, impersonation, and the fact that I did not intend the scammer to receive funds. The bank ignored Regulation XXXX requirements for unauthorized transfers. The bank refunded the {$25.00} wire fee, acknowledging good faith, but refused to return the {$1000.00} that was allowed to leave the account after a fraud report and after account closure. Under Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ), a transfer is unauthorized if the consumer did not intend the person receiving the funds to receive them. I did not intend for the scammer to receive the wire, and Wells Fargo misclassified the transaction as authorized. I am requesting CFPB assistance because Wells Fargo misclassified this as an authorized transfer, failed to act on a fraud report, failed to disclose a pending wire, and allowed the loss to occur after being notified of fraud. I am requesting reimbursement of the {$1000.00} wire that was improperly allowed to post.
